title: Fender’s CEO seems to think your bandmates are just analog AI
slides: Can Fender's CEO replace your bandmates with analog AI?
New digital guitars track every note your band plays.
Their CEO claims mistakes are just raw data, not flaws.
Your next jam session could be produced by your instrument.
Test one: see if your band's sound becomes too machine-like.
thread_text:
1. Your bandmate is an AI?

Fender's new tech tracks every note live, turning mistakes into data for machine learning.

2. The data doesn't lie.

Your instrument learns your style, then suggests riffs—or even writes parts for your next session.

3. No more bad takes?

AI edits your playing in real time, smoothing errors before the crowd hears them.

4. But who's the artist?

When the guitar composes, do you still own the song—or does the algorithm?

5. Test it this week.

Record your next jam with AI assist and compare the feel. Does it sound alive or sterile?
video_script: It turns them into new riffs.
Test it and judge for yourself.

instagram.caption:
Your next bassist might be a cable. 🎸  
Fender’s CEO says new digital guitars track every note your band plays live—and feed mistakes into machine learning as “raw data.”  

The instrument learns your style, then suggests riffs or writes parts for you. It even smooths errors in real time, before the crowd hears them.  

For anyone recording or performing, this means the tool you play can now edit your take before you approve it.  

But if the guitar composes and fixes your flubs, where does your band’s sound end and the algorithm begin? 🎛️ Try one this week: record a jam with AI assist, then ask yourself if it still feels like yours. ⚡
